# R04 selected EOS skill events — design fixtures

[中文](README_cn.md) · [IsOS event owner contract](../../../../../docs/isos/interfaces/cores/events.md) · [Cursor owner contract](../../../../../docs/isos/develop/owner/log-cursors.md) · [EOS owner contract](../../../../../docs/eos/interfaces/events.md)

`cases.json` pins EOS SkillService `192fbfa6fbed1e9b6a20dd8dc95501625b02d081` and freezes 31 selected-child accept/reject cases plus ten P07 cursor scenarios. `python3 tests/fixtures/r04_skill_events/check_cases.py` checks fixture shape and a reference owner-policy validator; it does **not** run IsOS. The implementation tests exercise the selected EOS runtime branch and keep old P06 policy cases passing.

Positive cases include queued, running, completed, a selected `0..1` version with an empty dot segment, failed with an unknown physical outcome, failed with an unreaped worker, and the fixed stop failure. The empty-segment case records current P01/EOS producer compatibility while the separate pre-stop grammar gate remains open. The selected skill pin includes build metadata; neither a MuJoCo-only package field validator nor a lowercase-only version rule applies to it. Negative cases reject bridge/EGIA spoofing, wrong run, node claim, message/level/stage/reason mismatch, arbitrary `worker.*` suffix, internal error code, missing or extra fields, incorrect types, invalid pin and execution ID, raw PID spoofing, stop-field drift, shared suppression and an unknown guest event code. The selected EOS role, not a graph or child capability claim, is the only source of authority.

For the cursor scenarios, submit each accepted raw event through a real selected EOS child pipe and confirm the exact sanitized record appears in both `eos.log` and `events.log` with IsOS's observed PID. A rejected event appears in neither. Use a run whose first eligible record is a skill failure; queued/running records leave the anchor pending. Query `view=current` both unfiltered and with an excluding source or correlation filter: the anchor remains the failure. A later accepted event with the same code must appear as a separate position after the anchor. Cross a retained backup with the old cursor (`rotated:true`, no loss), then expire the segment (`log_cursor_expired`, sealed anchor retained). Inject an intake/write gap, report the known count or null, and retain the final run after Stop. Use status for live readiness. Save the full replay and log-rotation output under ignored `logs/test/<run-id>/`.

The selected-skill P01 pin limit (96-byte package ID, 64-byte version and owner grammar) must also be enforced in IsOS candidate preflight before an active deployment is stopped. That preflight is a separate remaining implementation gate. EOS worker reap and R06 physical stop ordering require their own evidence; a log line never proves an actuator stopped.
